clue.text: Holds wrapping papers for children with bows

definitions.note: plural noun phrase: cherubs armed with bows and arrows

indicators.note: the holding word goes around the papers, enclosing them like a wrapper

parts.note: cups as a verb: holds in cupped hands

explanation.surface: Someone holds gift wrap for youngsters whose presents are tied with ribbons.
explanation.walkthrough: The bows look like ribbons on parcels, but they are archers' bows.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupids are winged infant figures of Roman love myth, each carrying an archer's bow and arrows.

clue.text: Opportunities to secure large areas for the cloth

indicators.note: the opportunities word holds the large letter inside it

explanation.surface: Chances to obtain big spaces for fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: The cloth is a term for the clergy, not fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancels are the parts of a church near the altar, reserved for clergy and choir.

clue.text: Something eaten in Iberia includes T bone

indicators.note: the Spanish dish contains the letter within it

parts.note: paella is a Spanish rice dish

explanation.surface: A Spanish meal includes a T-bone steak.
explanation.walkthrough: T-bone steak is split: T is a letter and bone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the kneecap, a small bone at the front of the knee.

clue.text: French state made economies after mounting waste

indicators.note: in a down entry, mounting means climbing, so the letters read from bottom to top
the economies word comes after the French state

explanation.surface: France made cuts after rising waste.
explanation.definitionFit: To devastate is to lay waste, to ravage and destroy.

clue.text: Flies pensioner removed from soap dishes from Asia

indicators.note: the pensioner's letters are taken out of the word soap, leaving only its first letter

parts.note: curries are spiced dishes from South Asia

explanation.surface: A retiree is taken off a TV soap opera, while Asian dishes are mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP, old-age pensioner, is a British term for a retired person.
explanation.definitionFit: To scurry is to hurry along quickly, which is one sense of the verb fly.

clue.text: Student players of revolutionary computer game down south

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the computer word goes backwards

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer

explanation.surface: A groundbreaking video game goes down well in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: Computer game looks like a single item but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge Blues are university students who have represented Cambridge at sport against Oxford.

clue.text: Behind spymaster, ready for battle again

parts.note: M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: Backing a spy chief, prepared to fight once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearm is to equip with weapons again, preparing for renewed fighting.

clue.text: This person's lost colour, getting stuck

parts.note: the setter speaking: I'm, I am

explanation.surface: Someone loses their colour after being stabbed.
explanation.walkthrough: This person's stands for the setter's I'm, with the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaled means pierced through with a stake, so stuck through.

clue.text: Make no comment on Liverpool strips

parts.note: sh is a call for silence
the Reds is the nickname of Liverpool FC

explanation.surface: Stay quiet about Liverpool's football kits.
explanation.walkthrough: Strips are football kits in British usage, but here the word means torn pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Shreds are narrow torn pieces, ragged strips of material.

clue.text: Republican opponent of government punched by dramatic Athenian

indicators.note: the Athenian punches a hole into the rebel's word and sits within it

parts.note: Timon of Athens is a Shakespeare play

explanation.surface: A rebel is struck by a theatrical Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: A republican, in the British sense, opposes rule by a monarchy.

clue.text: Supply item on van for detox treatment

indicators.note: read as supple, bendy, so these letters flex into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A delivery van brings an item for someone undergoing detox.
explanation.walkthrough: Supply looks like a verb but is read as the adverb of supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Antivenom is the serum given to neutralise a snake's poison, a literal detoxifying remedy.

clue.text: According to salesman, it comes from the east

indicators.note: in an across entry, coming from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
it is a crossword shorthand for sex appeal, SA

explanation.surface: A salesman claims his product is imported from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase as per is a common way of saying in accordance with someone's instructions or account.

clue.text: Whoppers from firm hiding investments, primarily

parts.note: a hiding is a heavy defeat, a loss

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A firm conceals its investments to make huge profits.
explanation.walkthrough: Hiding looks like a containment signal but is a noun meaning a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi are gigantic statues or figures, so huge things, whoppers in the informal sense.

clue.text: Scruffy parliamentarian was in government circles

indicators.note: the ruling verb surrounds the parliamentarian, as a ring goes round something

explanation.surface: An untidy MP moved in the inner circles of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumpled clothes are creased and untidy, giving a dishevelled look.

clue.text: Climber has trouble around Namibia's borders

indicators.note: turned around: the trouble word is read backwards
takes just the outer letters of the country's name

parts.note: the country's name, possessive dropped, whose two end letters are its borders

explanation.surface: A mountaineer runs into difficulties at the edges of Namibia.
explanation.walkthrough: Climber suggests a mountaineer, but it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody vine of tropical forests that climbs up trees.

clue.text: US vets behave affectionately, scrubbing hospital

definitions.note: plural noun: vet is American shorthand for a veteran

indicators.note: scrubbing out means erasing, so the hospital letter goes

parts.note: hold hands, as a couple might

explanation.surface: American veterinarians are tender with their animals after cleaning up in a clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: Vets suggests animal doctors, but in American usage it means veterans; scrubbing suggests surgeons washing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hands are experienced people, the veterans of any trade.

clue.text: They supply scores of soldiers after retreat of artillery

indicators.note: the soldiers come after the reversed artillery
artillery's letters fall back, read in reverse

explanation.surface: Many troops follow after the guns withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: Scores looks like a large number of soldiers but means musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrangers adapt music, writing out parts and orchestrations for performers.

clue.text: Time inside half-hearted, inadequate bank

indicators.note: one of the two middle letters is lost from the heart of the word

parts.note: a ridge is a raised bank of earth

explanation.surface: A feeble, half-hearted riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is British slang for a prison sentence; it also sounds like breakfast oats.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing porridge is British slang for serving a sentence behind bars.

clue.text: Be very fond of line by outstanding English poet

explanation.surface: Adoring a line by a great English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Lovelace was a seventeenth-century Cavalier writer, author of To Althea, from Prison.

clue.text: Banging on front of offices along with Jack

indicators.note: just the opening letter of offices

parts.note: taken as written, only its first letter used
a jack tar, a sailor, is a rating

explanation.surface: Knocking on the office door together with a man named Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: Banging on is British for talking at length tediously; a rating is a non-officer sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Orating is speechifying pompously, which is what banging on means.

clue.text: The odds for Real one cuts to 3 to 1, say

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word Real, first and third
the one cuts into the little word, sitting inside it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bookmaker's odds on Real Madrid winning are shortened to three to one.
explanation.walkthrough: Real looks like the Madrid football club; only its odd letters are wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A proportion expressed as three to one is an example of a numerical comparison.

clue.text: Police flipped after briefly hearing about a threesome

definitions.note: adjective phrase: relating to a group of three

indicators.note: the police letters follow the shortened hearing
cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing

indicators.note: flipped over in a down entry, read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Detectives lost their tempers after briefly hearing about a ménage à trois.
explanation.definitionFit: Triadic means relating to a triad, a group of three.

clue.text: Joint almost cracked very loudly

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, missing its last letter

explanation.surface: A joint nearly broke with a loud crack.
explanation.walkthrough: Joint suggests a body part or carpentry, but it is a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A spliff is slang for a hand-rolled cannabis cigarette.

clue.text: Still hoarding ultimate payment method

indicators.note: the photo word stores the other inside it, as a hoard is kept

parts.note: a still is a photograph, a pic

explanation.surface: Someone still hoards the best way to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Still reads as an adverb but is a noun, a single film frame or photo.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit and debit cards are known collectively as plastic, a common way to settle bills.

clue.text: Newspaper article supports ending of export tax

indicators.note: in a down entry, the supporting words sit below
takes the final letter of export

parts.note: taken as written, only its final letter used
the i is a British national newspaper

explanation.surface: A press article backs abolishing an export duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a levy of a tenth of produce paid to the church.

clue.text: Thinner mouchoir for cockney held in both hands

indicators.note: the handkerchief word sits between the two hand letters

parts.note: L and R, left and right
mouchoir is French for handkerchief; a cockney drops the H of hankie

explanation.surface: A cockney clutches a handkerchief in both hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, traditionally drop initial H sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Lankier means more tall and slim, so leaner and less stout.

clue.text: Dimwit using computers to grasp 500 + 10?

indicators.note: the computer letters hold the numbers between them

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
the digits 1 and 0 look like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: Someone stupid needs a computer to add 500 and 10.
explanation.walkthrough: The plus sign and question mark mock the sum; 10 is taken visually as the letters I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: How amazing heroine Verdi devised has inspired

indicators.note: inspired in its literal sense, breathed in, so the phrase holds the answer inside it

explanation.surface: An opera heroine created by Verdi has inspired others.
explanation.definitionFit: I never did is an exclamation of surprise, like well I never.

clue.text: More than one fancy suit is worn by law enforcers, along with sheriff's cap

indicators.note: the suit goes around the law enforcers like clothing on its wearers

parts.note: to fit, as in that suits you

indicators.note: a cap sits on top, so the first letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written, only its first letter used

explanation.surface: FBI men wear fancy suits and a sheriff wears a cap.
explanation.walkthrough: Fancy looks like an adjective for the suit but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Figments are inventions of the imagination, just as fancies are.

clue.text: Mind classic thriller film being given a new ending

indicators.note: the film title's last letter is swapped for a different one

explanation.surface: A classic Hitchcock thriller is given a different ending.
explanation.walkthrough: The replacement letter is not clued separately; the new ending must make a word meaning mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or spirit, the mind as an inner whole.
